examples.ko: 저 스님은 산에서 오래 수행하다가 득도했다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that monk attained enlightenment after long practice in the mountains.
You always speak calmly, like someone who has attained enlightenment.

examples.ko: 친구가 시험에 떨어지고도 웃길래 "득도했어요?" 하고 물었어요.
examples.en: My friend laughed even after failing the exam, so I asked, "Did you reach enlightenment?"

examples.ko: 그 이야기에서 주인공은 폭포 아래에서 명상하다가 득도해요.
examples.en: In that story, the main character meditates under a waterfall and attains enlightenment.

examples.ko: 몇 년을 수행해도 득도하기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Even after years of practice, attaining enlightenment is not easy.

examples.ko: 그렇게 매일 명상하면 저도 언젠가 득도할 수 있을까요?
examples.en: If I meditate every day like that, could I attain enlightenment someday too?

explain: 원래는 불교 수행으로 깨달음을 얻는다는 진지한 말이지만, 일상에서는 화를 안 내거나 욕심이 없는 사람에게 농담으로 '득도했네'라고 많이 말해요. 일반적인 사실을 알게 될 때는 '깨닫다'를 쓰고, '득도하다'는 큰 깨달음에만 써요.
explain_en: Originally a serious word for gaining enlightenment through Buddhist practice, but in daily life people jokingly say '득도했네' to someone who never gets angry or greedy. For simply realizing a fact, use '깨닫다'; '득도하다' is only for a big, deep enlightenment.

examples.ko: 요즘 가짜 뉴스의 득세가 큰 문제예요.
examples.en: The rise of fake news is a big problem these days.

examples.ko: 거짓 소문의 득세를 걱정하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people worry about the rise of false rumors.

examples.ko: 어느 시대에나 힘 있는 사람들의 득세는 있었어요.
examples.en: In every era, the powerful have had their time on top.

examples.ko: 새 기술의 득세로 옛 가게들이 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: With the rise of new technology, old shops are closing.

examples.ko: 요즘은 개인 방송의 득세가 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The dominance of personal broadcasts is noticeable these days.

examples.ko: 공정하지 않은 방법의 득세는 오래가지 않아요.
examples.en: The dominance of unfair methods doesn't last long.

explain: 주로 못마땅하거나 좋지 않은 것이 힘을 얻어 판을 칠 때 써요. 'A의 득세'처럼 앞에 힘을 얻은 것을 붙이고, 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '판치다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used when something undesirable gains power and takes over. It is used like 'A의 득세' (the rise of A) and appears often in news and writing. In everyday talk people also say '판치다'.

examples.en: These days, false information is gaining ground online.
When corrupt officials held power, the people suffered.

examples.ko: 득세한 사람들이 늘 오래가는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: The people who gain power don't always last.

examples.ko: 불공정한 방식이 득세하는 사회는 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: A society where unfair methods prevail can't last long.

examples.ko: 한때 득세했던 브랜드도 지금은 보기 어려워요.
examples.en: Even brands that were once dominant are hard to find now.

examples.ko: 거짓말이 득세하고 정직한 사람이 손해 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: We can't let lies prevail while honest people lose out.

explain: '득세하다'는 대개 좋지 않은 사람이나 생각이 힘을 얻어 세상을 휘두를 때 써서, 칭찬하는 말로는 잘 안 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '판치다'가 더 자연스럽고, '득세하다'는 뉴스나 글, 역사 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is usually used when bad people or ideas gain power and push things around, so it is rarely a compliment. In daily talk '판치다' sounds more natural, while '득세하다' shows up in news, writing and history stories.

examples.en: It's the summer holiday season, so the beach is teeming with people.
That old warehouse was swarming with rats.

examples.ko: 벌레가 득실거리는 곳에서는 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: I can't sleep in a place crawling with bugs.

examples.ko: 주말 시장에는 관광객이 득실거리고 정말 시끄러워요.
examples.en: The weekend market is packed with tourists and really noisy.
This website is crawling with ads.
During the holidays, every place will be swarming with people.

explain: '장소에 + 사람·벌레·쥐가 + 득실거리다'로 말하고, 많이 모여 어수선하거나 불쾌한 느낌이 있어요. 좋은 느낌 없이 가볍게 '많다'고 할 때는 '바글바글하다'가 더 일상적이에요.
explain_en: It follows the pattern 'place + 에 + people/bugs/rats + 이/가 + 득실거리다' and carries a messy or unpleasant feeling about the crowd. For a lighter, more casual 'crowded', '바글바글하다' is more common in daily speech.

examples.en: My younger brother who got first place is full of pride.

examples.ko: 그는 득의양양한 표정으로 상장을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: He showed the certificate with a triumphant look.
He walked off with his shoulders back, looking puffed up.
He was very full of himself because he got promoted.

examples.ko: 득의양양해서 자랑을 늘어놓더니 친구들이 질려 버렸어요.
examples.en: He went on bragging so smugly that his friends got fed up.
The kid who got the quiz answer right looks so pleased with himself.

explain: 원하던 일이 잘되어서 우쭐하고 자랑스러운 모습을 말해요. 칭찬이라기보다 '좀 으스댄다'는 느낌이 섞일 때가 많아요. '의기양양하다'와 비슷하게 쓰고, 말할 때는 '우쭐하다'가 더 가벼워요.
explain_en: It describes someone who is proud and cocky because things went well. It is often less a compliment than a hint of showing off. It is used much like '의기양양하다', and '우쭐하다' is a lighter word in speech.

examples.en: The residents rose up against the construction.
The reason the citizens rose up is simple.
The students rose up in protest, and the school was in an uproar for a while.

examples.ko: 요금이 또 오르면 소비자들이 들고일어날 거예요.
examples.en: If the fees go up again, consumers will rise up.
The news showed workers rising up in protest.
All the staff are rising up against the unfair treatment.

explain: 여러 사람이 함께 거세게 반발하거나 맞서 일어날 때 써서, 혼자 항의하는 상황에는 어색해요. '항의하다'보다 기세가 세고 말하는 느낌이 있어요. '들고 일어나다'로 띄어 쓰지 않고 한 단어로 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It is used when many people push back strongly together, so it sounds odd for one person complaining. It feels more forceful and spoken than '항의하다'. It is written as one word, '들고일어나다', without a space.

examples.en: Let's meet at the trailhead tomorrow morning.
Where is the entrance to the park walking trail?

examples.ko: 마을 들머리에 큰 나무가 한 그루 서 있어요.
examples.en: A big tree stands at the entrance of the village.
It takes about twenty minutes by bus to get to the trailhead.

examples.ko: 우리는 숲길 들머리를 찾느라 한참 헤맸어요.
examples.en: We wandered around for a while looking for the start of the forest path.

examples.ko: 이 길은 들머리는 좁은데 안쪽은 넓어요.
examples.en: This path is narrow at the start but wide inside.

explain: 주로 등산로나 산책길, 마을처럼 길이 시작되는 곳을 가리켜요. 건물이나 가게 입구에는 '입구'를 쓰는 게 자연스러워요. 반대로 길이 끝나 내려오는 곳은 '날머리'라고 해요.
explain_en: It mainly refers to where a hiking trail, walking path or village begins. For the entrance of a building or shop, '입구' is more natural. The opposite, where the path ends and you come out, is '날머리'.

examples.en: My mom keeps nagging me to study for the exam.
Please don't hassle the child so much.

examples.ko: 상사가 하루 종일 들볶는 바람에 지쳤어요.
examples.en: My boss hounded me all day, so I'm worn out.
I kept pestering my little brother and he ended up crying.
If you hassle me like that, I'll end up not wanting to do it.
My friend complains that her husband nags her about the housework.

explain: 잔소리나 재촉으로 상대를 계속 귀찮고 힘들게 할 때 써요. 한 번 때리거나 크게 괴롭히는 것보다 끈질기게 시달리게 하는 느낌이에요. 당하는 쪽에서 말하면 '들볶이다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when someone keeps bothering another person with nagging or pushing. The feeling is persistent harassment rather than one big act. From the receiving side, you say '들볶이다'.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 상사에게 들볶여서 너무 피곤해요.
examples.en: I was hounded by my boss all day, so I'm exhausted.
I get nagged by my parents every exam season.

examples.ko: 회의에서 들볶이는 날은 밥도 맛이 없어요.
examples.en: On days when I get hassled in meetings, even food tastes bad.
Yesterday I was pestered by the kids.

examples.ko: 이렇게 계속 들볶이면 아무것도 못 하겠어요.
examples.en: If I keep getting hassled like this, I can't do anything.
I was pressed so hard about the deadline yesterday that I finally blew up.

explain: '들볶다'의 피동형으로, 누군가의 잔소리나 재촉에 시달릴 때 써요. 사람에게는 '~에게/한테 들볶이다'로 말하고, 일에 시달릴 때는 '마감에 들볶이다'처럼 '에'를 쓰기도 해요. '시달리다'와 비슷하지만 들볶이다는 계속 닦달당하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is the passive form of '들볶다', used when you suffer under someone's nagging or pushing. For a person, say '~에게/한테 들볶이다'; for work pressure, '에' works too, as in '마감에 들볶이다'. It is close to '시달리다' but stronger in the feeling of being constantly pressed.

examples.en: If you inhale slowly, your mind relaxes.
In yoga, inhaling and exhaling are very important.

examples.ko: 들숨에 배를 내밀고 날숨에 넣어 보세요.
examples.en: Push your belly out as you inhale and pull it in as you exhale.
If your inhale is short, you run out of breath quickly.
Breathe in through your nose and out through your mouth.

examples.ko: 들숨보다 날숨을 길게 쉬면 긴장이 풀려요.
examples.en: If you breathe out longer than you breathe in, tension eases.

explain: 반대말은 '날숨'이고, 호흡 운동이나 명상, 노래 수업 같은 설명에서 자주 나와요. 평소 대화에서는 '숨을 들이쉬다'와 '숨을 내쉬다'라고 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '날숨', and it often appears in explanations for breathing exercises, meditation and singing lessons. In everyday talk people more often say '숨을 들이쉬다' and '숨을 내쉬다'.

en: move up and down; raise and lower

examples.ko: 신나는 음악이 나오자 어깨가 저절로 들썩거려요.
examples.en: When lively music plays, my shoulders bounce on their own.
The floor shook from the thumping next door.
The child waited, fidgeting on the chair.
On World Cup days, the whole country is abuzz.
Please sit still and don't keep fidgeting.
The pot lid is rattling as the noodles boil.

explain: 몸이나 물건이 가볍게 위아래로 움직일 때 써요. 어깨, 엉덩이, 냄비 뚜껑뿐 아니라 '온 나라가 들썩거리다'처럼 분위기가 들뜬 모습에도 써요. '들썩이다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when a body part or an object moves lightly up and down, like shoulders, hips or a pot lid. It also describes an excited atmosphere, as in '온 나라가 들썩거리다'. '들썩이다' is a common way to say the same thing.

examples.ko: 머리를 직접 잘랐더니 길이가 들쑥날쑥 달라요.
examples.en: I cut my hair myself, and the lengths came out uneven.

examples.ko: 요즘 퇴근 시간이 들쑥날쑥이라 약속을 못 잡아요.
examples.en: The time I leave work is all over the place lately, so I can't make plans.

examples.ko: 글씨가 들쑥날쑥 써져서 보기 안 좋아요.
examples.en: The writing came out uneven and looks bad.
My test scores keep coming out up and down, and I'm worried.
The hedge has grown unevenly.

examples.ko: 제 한 달 수입은 늘 들쑥날쑥이에요.
examples.en: My monthly income is always irregular.

explain: 길이, 크기, 시간, 점수처럼 고르지 않고 들쭉날쭉한 모습을 말해요. 부사지만 '들쑥날쑥이에요'처럼 '이다'를 붙여 쓰기도 해요. '들쭉날쭉'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It describes things that are uneven or inconsistent, such as length, size, time or scores. Although it is an adverb, it can take '이다', as in '들쑥날쑥이에요'. '들쭉날쭉' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

examples.en: The weather has been unpredictable lately.

examples.ko: 들쑥날쑥한 출근 시간 때문에 생활이 불규칙해요.
examples.en: My irregular start times make my life irregular.
I'm upset because I cut my bangs unevenly.
My grades are inconsistent, so it's hard to set a goal.

examples.ko: 가게 문 여는 시간이 참 들쑥날쑥하네요.
examples.en: The shop's opening hours are really irregular.
Last month's sales were quite uneven.

explain: 일정하지 않고 이랬다저랬다 하는 상태를 말해서, 날씨, 시간, 성적, 컨디션에 두루 써요. 모양이 고르지 않을 때도 쓰고, 보통 '불규칙하다'보다 말투가 편해요. '들쭉날쭉하다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It describes a state that is not steady and keeps changing, so it fits weather, schedules, grades and condition. It also works for uneven shapes, and sounds more casual than '불규칙하다'. '들쭉날쭉하다' can be used with the same meaning.
